covered_actors: Providers of general-purpose AI models placing models on the Union market
Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risks
Providers of general-purpose AI models released under free and open-source licenses
Downstream entities modifying or fine-tuning general-purpose AI models that become providers
compliance_deadlines: 2025-08-02: Obligation to publish the public summary of training content becomes applicable for general-purpose AI models placed on the Union market (no later than when the model is placed on the market).
2026-08-02: Enforcement actions by the AI Office for failure to publish the summary commence.
2027-08-02: Deadline for providers of general-purpose AI models placed on the market before 2 August 2025 to make the corresponding summaries available.
Six-month intervals (or sooner if a materially significant update is required): Update cadence for the summary when a model is further trained on additional data.
penalties_summary: Failure to publish the mandatory training content summary may lead to enforcement actions by the AI Office as of 2 August 2026, including fines of up to 3% of the provider's annual total worldwide turnover in the preceding financial year or EUR 15,000,000, whichever is higher.
implementation_notes: This document is an official European Commission FAQ explaining the mandatory Template for public summaries of training content under Article 53(1)(d) of the EU AI Act. Although the underlying statutory duty and use of the Template are mandatory, this FAQ itself is interpretive regulatory guidance rather than enacted legislation. The publication_date reflects the webpage's last update date (26 March 2026). The FAQ details three required summary sections, trade-secret balancing, SME thresholds for listing scraped domains (top 5% or 1,000 domains, whichever is lower, versus top 10% for other providers), and rules for justifying information gaps for models placed on the market before 2 August 2025.
